output.review_comment:
Two of the changes are good. The range check on `p` is fine, and so is the switch to the nearest-rank method (`ceil(p/100*n)`, with rank at least 1). Both follow the docstring.

The special case for `p == 50` with an even-length input can't be merged. It exists only to make `test_median_response_time` pass, and the PR description admits it goes against the docstring. The docstring says to use nearest rank with no interpolation and says the result is always one of the input values. The new branch interpolates and can return a value that isn't in the input (135 from [.., 120, 150, ..]). It also creates a jump: p=50 behaves differently from p=49.9 or p=50.1, and differently for odd and even `n`. The teammate said the docstrings are the source of truth, so the test is what's wrong here, not the function.

Please remove that branch and keep the pure nearest-rank logic. Then report that `test_median_response_time` expects 135, which contradicts the documented behavior (nearest rank gives 120), and let the team decide whether to fix the test or change the spec. Don't make the test pass silently. Also check that `math` is imported, because the diff doesn't add the import. If it's missing, the new code fails with a NameError.
